# Results — Study 858 (Margin ÷ Inventory Divergence)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
**Abarbanell–Bushee** contradiction: a rising gross margin while inventory grows faster than
sales is incoherent and forecasts weakness, so long the clean (positive-divergence) names and
short the contradictory (negative) ones. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python
examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar
month; the partial current month is dropped). Prices Fingerprint `bc81e3fc2938` (yfinance daily
adjusted closes); events cache = 957 (ticker, filing) rows.*

Run stamp: as-of 2026-06-30 · Fingerprint `bc81e3fc2938`.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **40** inventory-carrying US names with usable EDGAR history (of a 46-name fixed, current-survivors basket: retailers, manufacturers, consumer-staples, apparel, hardware/semis, autos) |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: quarterly `Revenues`/`CostOfRevenue` (+ tag fallbacks) and `InventoryNet`; de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **957** (ticker, quarter) events, period ends **2009-06-30 → 2026-05-03**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 46 names, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `divergence` = (ΔGross-margin%) − (inventory-growth − sales-growth), all YoY, all point-in-time |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh signals into **terciles**, long top (clean) / short bottom (contradictory), earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** The quarterly (60–100-day span) filter drops the fiscal-Q4
figure disclosed only as a full-year span in the 10-K, and six basket names lack enough
matched Rev/Cost/Inventory history to survive, so the per-name series has gaps and the monthly
cross-section is uneven (avg ≈19.9 names pre-2016, ≈17.0 after). No survivorship correction: the
basket is current survivors — named on the Signal axis, and it excludes exactly the glutted
retailers/OEMs an inventory-contradiction short would want (a bias that works *against* the
claim).

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does the divergence sort returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `divergence`, one execution lag, 2009-11 → 2026-06
(**200 months**, avg cross-section 18.0 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **−8.1 bps/month** (−0.97%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | −0.20 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **−0.18** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | −0.05 |
| monthly hit rate | 51% |
| long leg / short leg | +180.9 / +189.0 bps/month |

The primary long-short is **a slightly wrong-signed null** (NW *t* = −0.18). It is not even
sign-stable: the **staleness-120** variant flips to +4.7 bps/month (NW *t* = +0.09), and the
classic **inventory-vs-sales gap alone** (long the low-gap names) is +19.7 bps/month but only
NW *t* = +0.43. Every specification lands within a whisker of zero. There is no return sort in
this signal on this tape.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by signal)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `divergence`; top-minus-bottom forward drift, entered one
day after the filing:

| horizon | n | top | bottom | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 952 | +1.53% | +0.82% | **+0.71%** | +1.09 | 52% | 0.115 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 946 | +5.78% | +4.75% | **+1.03%** | +0.72 | 50% | 0.201 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 942 | +12.39% | +9.13% | **+3.26%** | +1.34 | 52% | 0.058 |

Right-signed but **flat and non-monotone**: the 63-day terciles run +4.75% / +3.07% / +5.78%
(low→high — the *middle* is the worst), the 126-day terciles +9.13% / +6.58% / +12.39%, the
long-short *t* never exceeds +1.34, and the label-shuffle placebo *p* sits at 0.06–0.20 (a
random tercile split beats the real one one time in six to one in five). A faint right-signed
whiff, nowhere near the desk's bar.

## Era split — the sign is not even stable across regimes

Calendar long-short, split at 2016-01-01 (≈ halves the calendar sample):

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| pre-2016 | 74 | **+18.6 bps** | +0.30 |
| 2016-2026 | 126 | **−23.8 bps** | −0.39 |

The long-short is **right-signed in the first half and wrong-signed in the second**, neither
half remotely significant. This is the signature of noise, not a decayed edge.

## The mechanism doesn't hold either — divergence does **not** lead future margin

Abarbanell–Bushee's own claim is that the contradiction predicts the *fundamentals*: the
low-divergence (contradictory) names should go on to suffer a gross-margin markdown. Pooled OLS
of **next year's** gross-margin change on this quarter's divergence (n = 834 matched events):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope *b* | **−0.000** |
| *t* (iid-pooled) | −0.74 |
| R² | 0.001 |
| Pearson correlation | **−0.026** |
| next-yr margin change, top divergence tercile | +0.23 pp |
| next-yr margin change, bottom divergence tercile | +0.79 pp |
| tercile spread | **−0.56 pp** (wrong-signed) |

Essentially zero, and if anything the *wrong* way: the contradictory (bottom) names go on to
post a slightly *larger* margin gain than the clean ones. Unlike the deferred-revenue study
(798), where the accounting lead was bulletproof even though the return spread was a null, here
**neither** the return sort **nor** the underlying accounting mechanism shows up on this panel.
Mean reversion in gross margin swamps whatever the divergence was supposed to signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + signal panel with a TUNABLE planted effect (high-divergence names drift
up); no network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **−0.02** (sd 0.92), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **1/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 858) | **+6.15** (mean +141.3 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (one borderline crossing in twelve HAC *t*'s, as chance
gives) and lights up hard on a planted effect. The real-tape NW *t* = −0.18 is therefore a
genuine null, not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.16):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | −15.6 bps/mo | −1.87%/yr | −0.34 | −0.09 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | −23.0 bps/mo | −2.76%/yr | −0.51 | −0.14 |

The gross edge is a wrong-signed null; costs and borrow only drive it further negative. There
is nothing to trade.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The primary calendar long-short is a **slightly wrong-signed null** (NW
  *t* = −0.18, one-sample −0.20) and is not even sign-stable: staleness-120 flips to +0.09, the
  era split runs +18.6 bps (pre-2016) then −23.8 bps (post), and the pooled event drift is
  right-signed but **flat, non-monotone, and placebo-insignificant** (*t* ≤ +1.34, *p* ≈
  0.06–0.20). No specification clears — or even approaches — the *t* = 2 bar. The
  Abarbanell–Bushee contradiction does not sort returns on this tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Negative gross, negative net (NW *t* = −0.34 to −0.51, Sharpe ≈
  −0.1). No paycheck for a spread that is worse than zero before costs.
- **Does it lead the fundamentals? — NO.** The divergence does **not** predict next year's
  gross-margin change (correlation −0.03, wrong-signed −0.56 pp tercile spread). The one thing
  that could have salvaged a "real information, no alpha" story — a genuine accounting lead —
  is also absent. A clean negative result on a famous, heavily-mined fundamental signal.
